meetings.title: Meeting Long Stress Test
meetings.transcript:
**Meeting Date**: April 4th, Q2 Strategy & Planning Kickoff
**Attendees**: Sarah (Project Manager), Mark (Engineering Lead), Jessica (Marketing), David (Design), Alex (Sales Director)

Sarah: Alright everyone, thanks for hopping on. We have a lot to cover today. The main goal is to finalize the roadmap for the Q2 product launch, specifically the enterprise features. We have an hour, so let's keep it moving. Alex, I know Sales has been clamoring for the new RBAC (Role-Based Access Control) feature.
Alex: Yeah, we're literally losing deals because we don't have enterprise-grade permissions. The client from last week, Acme Corp, specifically said they won't sign until we can guarantee custom admin roles.
Mark: I get it, but RBAC is a massive architectural shift. We can't just slap it on. The database migrations alone are going to take my team at least three weeks to map out safely.
Sarah: Understood. But we need a commitment. Can we have RBAC in staging by May 15th?
Mark: May 15th... If I pull two engineers off the reporting dashboard, yes.
Sarah: Let's do that. The reporting dashboard is a lower priority right now anyway. Decision made: we are pausing the reporting dashboard and going all-in on RBAC for a May 15th staging target.
Alex: Awesome. I'll let the Acme Corp reps know today that it's officially on the roadmap for Q2.
Jessica: Wait, if we're pushing RBAC, the marketing materials for Q2 are completely wrong. I've got a whole campaign drafted around the reporting dashboard. I'm going to have to scrap the whole thing and rewrite the enterprise landing page.
David: I can help with the landing page redesign. I'll need the new copy first, though.
Jessica: Give me until next Tuesday to get the new copy done.
David: Okay, if you get it to me by Tuesday, I can have the mockups for the RBAC landing page done by next Friday, the 14th.
Sarah: Perfect. So Jessica is on copy by Tuesday, David is on mockups by Friday.
Alex: What about the pricing? If we're adding enterprise RBAC, we need to finalize the new Enterprise Tier pricing. Who's owning that?
Sarah: Good point. We should definitely run a competitive analysis on how our competitors price their enterprise tiers. Someone needs to pull that data and draft a proposal.
Alex: I can't do it, I'm traveling for conferences all next week.
Jessica: I'm buried in rewriting this campaign now.
Sarah: We'll figure it out. Let's just leave it unassigned for now, but we need that competitive pricing analysis done before the end of the month. We'll revisit it on our next sync.
Mark: Real quick, on the technical side, the current AWS server costs are getting out of hand. We spiked by 40% last month. We need to do an infrastructure audit.
Sarah: Why did it spike so much?
Mark: We think it's the new automated backup system, but we aren't sure. I'll have someone on my team run an AWS cost audit. Let's say... by April 20th, we should have a report.
Sarah: Sounds good. Let's make sure that happens.
David: Also, totally off-topic, but the coffee machine in the breakroom is broken again. It's just dispensing hot water.
Alex: Yeah, it's been like that since Monday. It's a disaster.
Sarah: I'll slack the office manager about the coffee machine right after this call. I'm not putting that in the official meeting notes though!
Mark: Oh, one last thing on RBAC. We need to make sure the legal team updates the Terms of Service to reflect the new data boundaries.
Sarah: Good catch. Mark, since you know the technical boundaries, can you email legal the technical specs?
Mark: Sure, I'll email legal the technical specs for the ToS update by tomorrow EOD.
Sarah: Excellent. Anything else?
Alex: No, that's it for me. Go team!
Sarah: Thanks everyone. Let's get to work.
